note: Trigger-routing suite for the merged default-orchestration-protocol pack (ADR-0020 D5 / #524, 2026-08-17): team-or-solo-rules' composition/wiring-design cases folded in alongside the original #480 fleet-protocol cases (minted from the #373 overnight campaign). Positives span both classes the merged description now owns — the seven fleet-ops areas (coordination scope ladder, work-claim protocol, communication routing, version-slot/merge-order, session-death resilience, pin-race playbook, route-anything-incoming triage — the last added #577, 2026-08-17) and the composition-design class (unit choice, wiring review, dispatch shape). The two negatives that used to fence each half against the other (fleet-rules' n03/n04/n10 pointing at team-or-solo-rules; team-or-solo-rules' n13 pointing at fleet-rules) are removed as self-references post-merge, not renumbered into positives — the merged suite fences only against genuinely external siblings now: parallel-work-rules (isolation decision / live collision), loop-rules (continuation timing), mobilize-chores (which tickets are mobilizable), big-change-git-rules (stacked-PR/rename git mechanics, cross-plugin), agent-writing-rules (cross-plugin, encoding a delivery clause into an agent file), docs' file-bug/file-feature/file-task (cross-plugin — filing the record itself, never this skill's job, only naming WHERE), and harness's check-all-skills/check-all-agents/write-handoff/break-down-problem (corpus-wide sweeps and the handback contract, cross-plugin). Known accepted-leak class carried over from team-or-solo-rules (check-routing 2026-07-09): 'do my agents leverage the right skills' leaks here when check-all-agents (its owner, a user-only command) is off the model menu — benign; do not tune to chase it. 2026-08-17 (#581): n07/n16/n17/n18 audited as one candidate cross-plugin structural-leak class — each true owner (agent-writing-rules, check-all-agents, write-handoff, break-down-problem) lives in harness, absent from a teamwork-scoped menu. Description gained explicit NOT-lines for write-handoff and break-down-problem (agent-writing-rules and check-all-agents were already fenced). A fresh scoped check-routing re-run split the four: n07 and n16 remained real leaks (accepted, dated per-case above — the menu-scope limitation holds even with the fence in place, since the true owner is never a candidate for the judge to pick instead); n17 and n18 actually resolved to PASS — the new fences alone were enough to steer the judge to `none`, a real tune, not an accepted leak (dated per-case above). Same re-run's contested-vote round also caught t17/t18 as single-judge noise (dead on the first judge, 2-of-3 fleet-rules on the vote) unrelated to the day's edit — re-judged notes on both.
